questions.explain: Shabbat is the weekly day of rest from Friday evening to Saturday evening, recalling God resting after creation.

questions.q: Who was prepared to sacrifice his son Isaac in obedience to God?
questions.explain: Abraham showed faith when he was willing to sacrifice Isaac, before God provided a ram instead.

questions.q: Which festival is known as the Jewish Day of Atonement?
questions.explain: Yom Kippur is the Day of Atonement, the holiest day in the Jewish year, marked by fasting and prayer.

questions.q: During Sukkot, what do many Jewish families build and eat in?
questions.explain: During Sukkot families build a sukkah, a temporary hut recalling the Israelites' time in the wilderness.

questions.q: What event does the festival of Pesach (Passover) commemorate?
options: The Exodus from slavery in Egypt
questions.explain: Pesach commemorates the Israelites' escape from slavery in Egypt under Moses.

options: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible
questions.explain: The Torah is the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, central to Jewish teaching and law.

questions.q: With which figure did God first make the covenant in Judaism?
questions.explain: God made the original covenant with Abraham, promising land and many descendants.
Rosh Hashanah marks the Jewish New Year and the start of the High Holy Days.

questions.q: In Judaism, the Messiah is generally understood to be:
options: A symbol with no personal meaning
A future anointed leader who has not yet come
questions.explain: Most Jews believe the Messiah is a future human leader, anointed by God, who has not yet arrived.

questions.q: What is the building where Jews gather for communal worship called?
questions.explain: The synagogue is the Jewish place of communal worship, study and gathering.

questions.q: What does Judaism teach about the number of gods?
options: There are two equal gods, good and evil
questions.explain: Judaism is strictly monotheistic, believing in one God who is the creator of everything.

questions.q: How many mitzvot (commandments) does the Torah traditionally contain?
questions.explain: The Torah traditionally contains 613 mitzvot that guide Jewish life.
